facts.text: New Harmony was settled in 1862 by pioneers who were displaced after heavy rains destroyed the adobe walls of nearby Fort Harmony.
The town's name symbolizes unity and cooperation, drawing inspiration from Harmony, Pennsylvania, where Joseph Smith translated the Book of Mormon.
Early settlers in New Harmony attempted to mine and refine iron, even building a crude foundry in 1852.
The boundary of the Pine Valley Mountain Wilderness lies less than a mile outside of the New Harmony city limits.
New Harmony sits at an elevation of over 5,000 feet, allowing the local climate to display all four seasons year-round.
Archaeological excavations by Brigham Young University uncovered porcelain and structural remnants that reveal daily pioneer life at the old Fort Harmony site.
